newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mediator asks Japan to press Lima on crisis - report.
newsitem.headline: Mediator asks Japan to press Lima on crisis - report.

text.p: Catholic Archbishop Juan Luis Cipriani, a top mediator in the hostage standoff in Lima, has urged Japan to press Peru for a peaceful resolution of the four-month-old crisis, Japanese media reports said on Tuesday.

Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Sunday received a letter from Cipriani relayed by the Japanese diplomat who headed Japan's Lima hostage crisis task force until last week, Hashimoto told reporters.

Hashimoto declined to discuss the contents of the letter, but his aides were quoted by Kyodo news agency and other media as saying Cipriani urged Hashimoto to renew efforts toward a negotiated solution of the hostage crisis.

Cipriani's plea was possibly based on concern that hardliners in President Alberto Fujimori's government had increased their influence on Lima's crisis policy since the resignation of Interior Minister Juan Briones, one Hashimoto administration official told the daily Sankei Shimbun.

Cipriani, Red Cross official Michel Minnig and Canadian Ambassador Anthony Vincent make up the guarantors' commission which has served as an intermediary in delicate, behind-the-scenes talks between leftist rebels and Fujimori's government.

About 20 jungle-trained rebels of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) have held 72 captives, including the Japanese and Bolivian ambassadors, since they took over the ambassador's residence during a cocktail party on December 17.
The main sticking point in the negotiations has been the rebels' demand for the release of comrades held in top security jails throughout Peru.
Fujimori has steadfastly refused to free any convicted fighters, but sources have said he may consider sentence reductions for low-ranking MRTA prisoners.
